q.q: Why is the micro:bit described as a microcontroller?
o: It controls the other computers on a network
Its CPU, RAM and programmable inputs and outputs are all on a single board
It is too small to be a real computer
It can only be programmed with a microphone
q.why: A microcontroller is a mini computer with everything on a single board.

q.q: Which micro:bit sensor detects shaking?
q.why: The accelerometer detects movement such as shaking or tilting.

q.q: How many LEDs are on the front of the micro:bit?
q.why: The LEDs form a 5 × 5 grid, which is 25 LEDs.

q.q: Which of these is NOT needed for a device to count as a microcontroller?
q.why: Microcontrollers need CPU, RAM and programmable I/O on a single board, not a monitor or keyboard.

q.q: Why did the BBC design the micro:bit?
o: To let pupils watch BBC programmes
To act as a school network server
To encourage pupils to learn coding and programming skills
q.why: It was designed to encourage pupils to learn basic coding and programming skills.

q.q: In 2016, which year group in Northern Ireland was given a free micro:bit?
q.why: Every Year 7 pupil in England and Wales and the matching years in Scotland and NI (Year 8 here) got one.

q.q: What lets a micro:bit connect wirelessly to other micro:bits?
q.why: Bluetooth and radio let it connect to other micro:bits or devices.

q.q: Which of these is an example of a programmable input/output peripheral on a micro:bit?
q.why: Buttons, sensors and LEDs are programmable I/O peripherals; CPU and RAM are separate requirements.

q.q: What are the coordinates of the top-left LED?
q.why: Counting starts at 0 in the top-left corner.

q.q: Which LED is in the very centre of the grid?
q.why: Counting goes 0,1,2,3,4 so the middle is 2.

q.q: Which part lets you plug in extra sensors and devices?
q.why: The gold edge connector links to other devices and sensors.

q.q: Which parts were added in Version 2 of the micro:bit?
o: The USB connector and battery socket
q.why: V2 added a speaker, a microphone and a touch-sensitive logo.

q.q: Which code lights up the LED in the 4th column from the left and the 2nd row from the top?
q.why: Counting from 0: x = 3 is the 4th column, y = 1 is the 2nd row down.

q.q: What are the coordinates of the bottom-left LED?
q.why: x = 0 is the left column and y = 4 is the bottom row, because y counts down.

q.q: Apart from showing pictures, what else can the LED matrix sense?
q.why: The LED matrix can also sense light level.

q.q: What does the USB connector on the micro:bit do?
o: Powers it and loads programs from a computer
Connects extra sensors to the pins
Detects which direction it is facing
q.why: The USB connector connects to a computer to power it and load programs.

q.q: An older V1 micro:bit needs to play a tune. What is needed?
o: A battery pack in the battery socket
A second micro:bit connected by radio
Nothing, it has a built-in speaker
Headphones or a buzzer wired to the pins
q.why: Older V1 boards need headphones or a buzzer wired to the pins for sound.

q.q: Which LED is (4,0)?
q.why: x = 4 is the right-hand column and y = 0 is the top row.

q.q: You click Download in MakeCode. What do you then copy onto the MICROBIT drive?
o: A Word document of your code
q.why: Download makes a .hex file, which you copy to the MICROBIT drive to run.

q.q: What is the MakeCode simulator for?
o: Sharing a link to your project
Testing your code on screen before downloading
q.why: The simulator runs a virtual micro:bit so you can test your code.

q.q: Which block runs its code only once, when the micro:bit starts?
q.why: on start runs once when the micro:bit powers up; forever repeats.

q.q: Why does your hex file disappear from the MICROBIT drive after copying?
o: The micro:bit runs it and does not store other files
The copy failed and must be tried again
It was moved into My Documents
q.why: That is normal: the micro:bit only accepts hex files and does not store anything else.

q.q: What are the four steps to run a program on a micro:bit, in order?
o: Connect it, program it, download it, play it
Program it, play it, connect it, download it
Connect it, download it, program it, play it
Download it, connect it, program it, play it
q.why: Connect by USB, program in MakeCode, download the hex file, then copy it to play.

q.q: What happens to the yellow LED on the back while a hex file copies?
q.why: The yellow LED on the back flashes while it copies, then the code runs automatically.

q.q: What does the forever block do?
o: Runs its code only when a button is pressed
Runs its code once when the micro:bit starts
Runs its code over and over until the power is removed
Runs its code a set number of times
q.why: forever repeats until the power is removed.

q.q: Where in the MakeCode editor do you drag and snap blocks together?
q.why: The workspace is where you drag and snap blocks; the toolbox holds the block categories.

q.q: What is a string?
o: A piece of text: a sequence of characters
A number with a decimal point
A value that is either true or false
A whole number with no decimal point
q.why: A string holds text: any sequence of characters.

q.q: Which data type should store 3.75?
q.why: It has a decimal point, so it is a double.

q.q: Which data type can only be true or false?
q.why: Booleans have only two values.

q.q: In MakeCode's JavaScript view, what does # mean in a show leds picture?
q.why: In the JavaScript view # means the LED is on and . means it is off.

q.q: Why should a phone number such as 07700 900123 be stored as a string?
o: Integers cannot be shown on the micro:bit's LEDs
You never do maths with it and an integer would lose the leading 0
Strings are the only type that can hold more than five digits
Phone numbers contain a decimal point
q.why: You never do maths with it, and an integer would lose the leading 0.

q.q: What data type is "42" (with the quotation marks)?
q.why: Text in quotation marks is always a string, even "42".

q.q: How do you make an animation on the micro:bit?
o: Put one show leds block inside on start
Put show number blocks inside on button A pressed
Put several show leds blocks one after another inside forever
Use a single show string block
q.why: Several show leds blocks inside forever play as an animation.

q.q: Which block scrolls text across the LEDs?
q.why: The show string block scrolls a string across the LEDs.

q.q: Which data type is best for the number of goals scored in a match?
q.why: Goals are whole numbers, so integer.

q.q: Which value is a character (char)?
q.why: A char is a single letter or symbol.

q.q: Which option runs code when both buttons are pressed together?
q.why: Choose A+B from the drop-down (Button.AB in JavaScript) to run code when both are pressed together.

q.q: Which block category holds the 'on button pressed' block?
q.why: Buttons are inputs, so it is in Input.

q.q: Why save a copy of your hex file in My Documents?
o: It makes the code run faster
The simulator needs it to run
The micro:bit does not keep the file
MakeCode deletes it after a day
q.why: The MICROBIT drive does not store files, so keep your own copy.

q.q: In buttonBashing, is the LED display an input or an output?
q.why: LEDs show information, so they are output.

q.q: Why is 'on button pressed' called an event?
o: It repeats a set number of times
Its code runs only when that button is pressed
Its code runs all the time
It runs once when the micro:bit starts
q.why: An event's code runs only when the event happens, not all the time.

q.q: In JavaScript, how is 'both buttons pressed' written?
q.why: In JavaScript the choices are Button.A, Button.B and Button.AB.

q.q: You extend buttonBashing with your own animation. Why save it as buttonBashingExtended?
o: Because hex files need a longer name
So it runs faster on the micro:bit
So you do not overwrite your first version
Because MakeCode does not allow the same name
q.why: Saving with a new name means you don't overwrite your first version.

q.q: Which is a sign of good file organisation in My Documents?
o: Files named Document1, Document2 and so on
All hex files saved straight onto the desktop
Every file saved in one big folder
A folder for each year with no orphan files lying loose
q.why: My Documents should contain a folder for each year, with subject folders and no loose files.

q.q: What does 'loop' mean in programming?
q.why: To loop means to repeat; choosing between options is selection.

q.q: Which is a count-controlled loop?
q.why: It runs a known number of times.

q.q: A while loop checks its condition when?
o: Only when a button is pressed
q.why: The condition is checked before each iteration.

q.q: In Activity 3, a for loop that runs 3 times shows 0 1 2 3, then 4 5 6 is shown. How many times does '0 1 2 3' appear before '4 5 6'?
q.why: The for loop runs 3 times before moving on to 4 5 6.

q.q: What is another word for a loop?
q.why: Loops are also called iteration.

q.q: myValue starts at 0. While myValue < 10, show myValue then add 1. What is the last number shown?
q.why: When myValue becomes 10, 10 < 10 is false so the loop stops before showing it.

q.q: What type of loop is the forever block?
o: A condition-controlled loop that checks a button
q.why: forever never stops while the micro:bit has power.

q.q: A while loop forgets to include myValue += 1. What happens?
o: The loop runs ten times then stops
The micro:bit shows an error and restarts
The loop never ends and the program gets stuck
q.why: If the condition never becomes false the loop never ends: an infinite loop.

q.q: What is another name for a count-controlled loop?
q.why: A count-controlled loop is also called a for loop; a condition-controlled loop is a while loop.

q.q: Why would you use a while loop instead of a repeat loop?
o: You want it to run when a button is pressed
You don't know how many times it needs to run
You know exactly how many times it needs to run
You want it to run only once
q.why: Condition-controlled loops are used when the number of repeats is unknown.

q.q: In a game, the variable score changes from 0 to 3 as goals are scored. Why is it called a variable?
o: Its value can change while the program runs
It always holds the same value
It is a type of loop
q.why: A variable is a named store whose value can change.

q.q: Which block makes a random dice number?
q.why: A dice gives 1 to 6; the default 0 to 10 includes 0 and 7–10.

q.q: Which sensor detects the shake gesture?
q.why: The accelerometer detects movement.

q.q: A variable age = 15. A year later the program sets age = 16. What does this show?
q.why: That is why it is called a variable.

q.q: Why is pick random 0 to 10 wrong for a dice?
o: It always gives the same number
A dice has no 0 and no 7–10
q.why: The default block goes from 0 to 10; a dice has no 0 and no 7–10.

q.q: Which is the best name for a variable that stores the number of lives in a game?
q.why: Variable names should describe what they store; x makes code hard to follow.

q.q: score = 0. The player scores three goals and score goes up by 1 each time. What is score now?
q.why: The value changes each goal: 0 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

q.q: Why store the dice roll in a variable called roll instead of just showing it?
o: So the roll is always a 6
So the dice shows the number faster
So the micro:bit stores the hex file
So the value can be used again, e.g. to check for a 6
q.why: Storing the roll in a variable means you can use it again.

q.q: In the RollTheDice program, what triggers the roll?
q.why: input.onGesture(Gesture.Shake) is an event triggered by the accelerometer.

q.q: When does the code inside an if block run?
q.why: The code inside an if runs only when its condition is true.

q.q: What does else do?
o: Runs code when the condition is false
Repeats the code inside the if
q.why: else provides the alternative when the condition is false.

q.q: What is a Boolean?
o: A whole number, positive or negative
A loop that repeats until a button is pressed
A value that is either true or false
A piece of text in quotation marks
q.why: Booleans have only two values.

q.q: In the Lie Detector, what decides which message appears?
q.why: pick random true or false (Math.randomBoolean()) decides.

q.q: What is selection in programming?
o: Repeating code a set number of times
The program choosing which code to run
Storing a value in a variable
q.why: Selection means the program chooses which code to run, using if.

q.q: In which MakeCode block category is the if statement found?
q.why: if is in the blue-green Logic blocks.

q.q: What is computational thinking?
o: Thinking about how fast a computer is
Telling a computer exactly what to do, step by step
Letting the computer decide for itself
q.why: Computers can't think for themselves, so we tell them exactly what to do step by step.

q.q: In the Lie Detector, Math.randomBoolean() returns false. What is shown?
q.why: When the condition is false, the else part runs.

q.q: What is the result of 7 < 4?
q.why: 7 is not less than 4, so the comparison gives false.

q.q: Which operator means 'not equal to'?
q.why: != (≠) means not equal to; == means equal to.

q.q: Which of these is true?
q.why: 5 is equal to 5, so ≥ is true.

q.q: What does == do in code?
o: Sets a variable to a value
q.why: == tests whether values are equal; = sets a value.

q.q: What is the difference between score = 0 and score == 0?
o: = is used in JavaScript; == is used in blocks
They do exactly the same thing
= sets score to 0; == checks whether score is 0
= checks whether score is 0; == sets score to 0
q.why: A single = sets a variable; == compares.

q.q: What does a comparison operator always give as its result?
q.why: The result is always true or false.

q.q: lives = 0. Which condition is true?
q.why: 0 is less than or equal to 0, so lives <= 0 is true.

q.q: In the faces task, a = 1 and b = 0. Which condition is true?
q.why: a is 1 and b (0) is less than 1, so the first condition is true and the Happy face shows.

q.q: Which is NOT a use of comparison operators named in the notes?
q.why: Comparison operators are used in conditional statements, loops and sorting.

q.q: When is the output of an AND gate true?
o: Only when all inputs are true
q.why: AND needs every input true.

q.q: A = 0, B = 1. What is A OR B?
q.why: OR needs only one true input.

q.q: How many inputs does a NOT gate have?
q.why: NOT has a single input, which it inverts.

q.q: Which code checks that both button A and button B are pressed?
q.why: && is AND, so both must be pressed.

q.q: A = 1, B = 0. What is A AND B?
q.why: AND is only 1 when both inputs are 1.

q.q: What is NOT 0?
q.why: NOT inverts its input: 0 becomes 1.

q.q: Which symbol means OR in code?
q.why: OR is ||, AND is && and NOT is !.

q.q: myValue = 15. Is (myValue > 10 || myValue < 0) true or false?
o: false, because both parts must be true
true, because both parts are true
q.why: With OR only one part needs to be true; 15 > 10 is true.

q.q: In the OR task, neither button is pressed. What is shown?
q.why: Both inputs are false, so OR is false and the else part shows F.

q.q: In the NOT task, button A is being pressed. What number is shown?
q.why: buttonIsPressed is true, so NOT makes it false and the else part shows 0.

q.q: When is the output of a NOR gate true?
o: When at least one input is true
q.why: NOR is the opposite of OR: true only when both inputs are false.

q.q: What is 1 XOR 1?
q.why: XOR is true only when inputs differ.

q.q: What is NOT(1 AND 1)?
q.why: 1 AND 1 = 1, and NOT 1 = 0.

q.q: How many rows does a truth table for 2 inputs need?
q.why: Two inputs have four combinations: 00, 01, 10 and 11.

q.q: When is the output of a NAND gate false?
o: Only when both inputs are true
Only when both inputs are false
q.why: NAND is the opposite of AND: false only when both inputs are true.

q.q: What does a small circle on the output of a gate in a circuit diagram mean?
q.why: A small circle on the output means NOT.

q.q: What is 0 XOR 1?
q.why: The inputs are different, so XOR gives 1.

q.q: P = 1 and Q = 0. What is (P OR Q) AND R if R = 0?
q.why: P OR Q = 1, then 1 AND 0 = 0.

q.q: What is the best way to complete a truth table for a circuit with several gates?
o: Add a column for each gate and fill them left to right
Work out the whole circuit in your head at once
Only fill in the rows where the inputs are 1
Fill in the final output column first
q.why: Add a column for each gate in the middle and fill them left to right.

q.q: What is NOT(0 OR 0)?
q.why: 0 OR 0 = 0, then NOT 0 = 1: this is the NOR gate.
